content.text: {"label":"unknown_supply_issue","explanation":"The problem is on the supply side. Payments has 11 agents on phones against 17 planned, and general has 11 against 15. Attendance shows 9 payments and 8 general absences, against usual levels of about 2.5 per day. Most are logged as late because of a bus strike (8 in payments, 5 in general); only 1 payments and 3 general agents are sick, so this is not a sick wave. Demand is roughly on forecast: payments is up 8.4% today, with a spike at 08:15 led by payment_status_enquiry, and general is down 14.5%. The only incident, an overnight statement batch, is resolved, and the fraud-awareness social post does not go out until 11:25. A bus strike is not one of the listed causes, so I have used unknown_supply_issue. Payments service level fell to 38% at 08:15, with 10 calls abandoned.","plan_name":"Bridge the bus-strike staffing gap until late agents arrive","rationale":"Most absent agents are late rather than off for the day, so the gap should shrink over the morning. The plan uses free or cheap levers to cover the next 2–3 hours, with payments as the priority. Breaks in the morning window are pushed back and coaching is cancelled on both queues to put more agents on phones. Payments overtime is offered from 09:00 to 11:00, since agents arrive 30 minutes after approval. Ten offers at about 40% acceptance is roughly 4 agents for 2 hours, about Rs 2,880, well within the Rs 15,000 budget. Callbacks smooth the peaks on payments. Chat deflection of up to 20% of payment_status_enquiry calls targets the reason that is rising, at Rs 12 per chat.
